findings.title: Flex layout disables the right-aligned small-action button
findings.body: Making `.small-action` a flex container causes its direct child `button` to become a flex item. CSS floats do not apply to flex items, so the existing `float: right` on `.small-action button` is ignored. The button will now sit immediately after `.small-action-desc` rather than at the right edge, and long descriptions can leave it incorrectly positioned or squeezed. Add flex positioning such as `margin-left: auto` to the button (and appropriate sizing for the description) instead of relying on its float.

findings.title: Header panel loses its right alignment in legacy flexbox implementations
findings.body: The prior `float: right` was removed and replaced with `margin-left: auto` on a flex item. The legacy flexbox implementations targeted by the new `-ms-flexbox`/`-webkit-box` declarations, notably IE10's 2012 flexbox implementation, do not reliably support auto main-axis margins. In those browsers the panel will follow the title instead of being pushed to the right, potentially causing the header controls to overlap or overflow. Provide an old-flexbox-compatible alignment fallback (for example legacy box packing/flex sizing) or retain a non-flex fallback for these browsers.
